summary.headline: Sell measurable automation or security fixes before building software; evidence supports real SME scale and cyber pain, not guaranteed demand for any offer.
summary.best_opportunity: Fixed-scope cyber hygiene and recovery-readiness service for small UK firms, with recurring checks.
summary.why_now: The live GOV.UK 2025 Cyber Security Breaches Survey reports 43% of businesses experienced a breach or attack in the prior 12 months; UK business population estimates count 5.7m private-sector firms, 5.64m small. This points to a widespread problem and reachable market, but does not prove willingness to pay; start with a tightly scoped, non-regulated assessment and test sales directly.

top_opportunities.name: Cyber hygiene and recovery-readiness setup for small firms
top_opportunities.description: Provide a fixed-scope review of MFA, backups, patching, account access and incident contacts; implement agreed basic fixes and offer monthly checks. Avoid claiming certification or specialist penetration testing.
top_opportunities.why_now: GOV.UK Cyber Security Breaches Survey 2025 reports 43% of businesses experienced a breach or attack in the previous 12 months. This is a credible pain signal, not proof that small firms will buy this specific service.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small professional-services firms and local businesses without in-house IT/security staff.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £150–£700 for insurance research, secure checklist/tools, domain and basic sales materials; exclude founder time.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–3 weeks if sold as a paid assessment through direct outreach and referrals.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monthly backup/MFA/access reviews and remediation support; medium if the initial work creates clear ongoing value.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Good technical fit, but requires security competence, careful scope and appropriate insurance; do not represent this as a penetration test.
risks: Trust, liability and professional-indemnity requirements may exceed a part-time solo operator's comfort or budget.
Buyers may rely on existing IT providers or resist paying for preventative work.

scores.demand: 4/5 — strong incident prevalence signal; buyer conversion unverified
scores.startup_ease: 3/5 — requires secure process, clear scope and insurance review
scores.founder_fit: 3/5 — technical fit depends on demonstrated security capability

top_opportunities.verdict: Best evidence-led test only if security expertise and liability cover are adequate; otherwise partner with an MSP and sell a narrow, supervised workflow.

top_opportunities.name: Missed-enquiry recovery for home-service businesses
top_opportunities.description: Configure enquiry capture, rapid acknowledgement, lead qualification and booking handoff using existing tools; charge setup plus ongoing monitoring.
top_opportunities.why_now: GOV.UK estimates 5.7m UK private-sector businesses at the start of 2025, 5.64m small. The market scale is real, but no current source establishes trade-specific demand; validate missed enquiries with prospects before building.
top_opportunities.buyer: Independent plumbers, electricians, roofers and other appointment-led trades.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £100–£600 for a demo, domain, messaging and automation tools; exclude founder time.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–3 weeks if sold directly as a fixed-scope pilot.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monthly monitoring, changes and usage administration; medium-high if recovered leads are measurable.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong engineering and integration fit; requires practical sales and consent-aware messaging.
risks: Crowded CRM/automation market; differentiation must be a trade-specific outcome.
Messaging consent, data protection and brittle integrations require careful design and fallback.
top_opportunities.verdict: Strong low-cost pilot; interview buyers and secure payment before writing custom software.

top_opportunities.name: Website care and enquiry conversion package for local firms
top_opportunities.description: Fixed-scope website fixes, analytics and enquiry tracking plus a monthly maintenance and improvement plan.
top_opportunities.why_now: The GOV.UK 2025 estimate documents a large small-business base, while the direct local-service model permits immediate prospect testing. The population statistic does not establish unmet website demand.
top_opportunities.buyer: Local trades, clinics and independent professional services with dated sites or broken enquiry journeys.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £100–£500 using an existing web stack and low-cost hosting/tools.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 1–3 weeks with a prospect-specific audit and fixed-price scope.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monthly maintenance, edits and conversion reporting; moderate unless linked to leads or uptime.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong for a software engineer with web delivery experience.
risks: Price competition from agencies, freelancers and DIY builders.
Clients may churn if outcomes and scope are not measurable.
top_opportunities.verdict: Reliable fallback cash-flow service; sell fixes to conversion and enquiries, not redesign alone.

top_opportunities.name: AI-assisted document and admin workflow for small accountancy practices
top_opportunities.description: Automate one repetitive intake, document-chasing or triage workflow with human review, audit trail and explicit exception handling.
top_opportunities.why_now: A large UK small-business population is documented in GOV.UK's 2025 estimates, but current live evidence gathered here does not establish accountancy-practice buying urgency or a specific unmet workflow.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small UK accountancy and bookkeeping practices.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £200–£1,000 for a controlled prototype, secure tools and discovery.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 2–6 weeks after finding a practice partner and agreeing a low-risk pilot.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monthly support or per-workflow fee if it becomes operationally embedded.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Good technical fit; domain trust and data handling are constraints.
risks: Financial and personal data create confidentiality, privacy and security obligations.
Practice software may already cover the workflow; integration and exception cases can expand scope.
top_opportunities.verdict: Proceed only with a practice partner, a narrow human-reviewed workflow and explicit data controls.

top_opportunities.name: Micro-SaaS for a narrow operational or compliance reminder workflow
top_opportunities.description: A lightweight evidence and reminder tracker for one specific UK microbusiness segment, initially delivered manually to validate the workflow.
top_opportunities.why_now: A substantial SME base is documented by GOV.UK, but population size is not niche demand evidence; no validated workflow or buyer signal was established in this run.
top_opportunities.buyer: A narrowly selected microbusiness segment with repeated, costly admin tasks.
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £300–£1,500 for a minimal MVP, hosting and customer discovery.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: 4–12+ weeks; usually slower without distribution or pre-committed buyers.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Potentially high through subscription if retention and ongoing workflow value are proven.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: High engineering fit but weak immediate-cash fit until a niche is validated.
risks: Building before identifying paying customers risks wasted time and budget.
Incumbents, changing rules and support demands can undermine retention and margins.
top_opportunities.verdict: Do not build yet; seek paid manual pilots and only productise a repeated workflow.

best_pick.name: Cyber hygiene and recovery-readiness setup for small firms
best_pick.why_it_wins: The live 2025 government survey supplies a stronger current problem signal than generic SME market sizing alone. A bounded service can be tested without building software, but only pursue it within demonstrated competence and liability cover; otherwise the missed-enquiry automation offer is a safer technical-fit alternative.
validation_plan: Speak with 10 small firms and 3 local managed-service providers; ask what basic security checks customers request, what gaps recur and who currently owns remediation.

Offer a clearly scoped paid pilot to 2 firms only after confirming expertise, insurance and safe handling; measure completed fixes and customer willingness to renew rather than promising breach prevention.
best_pick.first_offer: A one-off £250–£500 basic cyber-hygiene and recovery-readiness review, with an optional £49–£149/month follow-up plan; test pricing, do not present it as an established market rate or formal security certification.
best_pick.mvp: A documented checklist covering MFA, backup restore evidence, software updates, account access and incident contacts; client-approved fixes, written limitations, secure evidence handling and referral/escalation to qualified specialists for advanced issues.
customer_types: Small professional-services firms without internal IT staff
Local businesses with customer records and no current managed-security support
best_pick.do_today: Check competence and professional-indemnity requirements first; then contact five local MSPs or small firms for discovery. If scope or insurance is unsuitable, test missed-enquiry recovery with trades instead.
